trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check into Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a leisurely walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — see Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Marvel at Gaudí's architecture without paying entry fees.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to Plaça de Catalunya to soak in the city atmosphere. Explore the lively streets of Eixample as the city comes alive. Head to a local bar for your first taste of Barcelona nightlife — try a classic 'vermut' (vermouth) at a neighborhood bar.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab a coffee and croissant at a local café near the hotel (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Grab a 'bocadillo' (sandwich) or slice of pizza from a local takeaway near Eixample (€4–7)
meals.dinner: Try the 'Menú del Día' (set menu) at a neighborhood restaurant near Passeig de Gràcia — typically 3 courses with bread and drink for €12–15

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport or any metro station — it will save money throughout the trip. August in Barcelona is hot (28–33°C), so carry water and wear sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Sagrada Família (book tickets online in advance — €26 basic entry, or €20 with student/youth discount). Arrive early (9:00–10:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, one of the world's most extraordinary pieces of architecture. The exterior alone is breathtaking if budget is tight — exterior viewing is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (€10 entry for the Monumental Zone — book online to avoid queues). Explore the colorful mosaic terraces, the famous dragon staircase, and Gaudí's whimsical architectural landscape. The surrounding park outside the paid zone is free and offers great city views. Afterward, head back to Eixample for a mid-afternoon rest during the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gràcia neighborhood on foot — a bohemian, artsy district full of charming plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Join locals for 'la hora del vermut' around 19:00. As night falls, check out the bars and small live music venues in Gràcia for an authentic, budget-friendly nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and 'pa amb tomàquet' (bread with tomato) at a local café near the hotel (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Park Güell — grab fresh produce, cheese, and local bread from a nearby Mercadona supermarket (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a casual tapas bar in Gràcia — order 'patatas bravas', 'croquetas', and 'pan con tomate' to share (€10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days in advance — they sell out quickly in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes as both sites involve significant walking and uneven terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — one of Barcelona's most atmospheric and historically rich neighborhoods. Explore the narrow medieval streets for free. Visit the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30 on weekdays), the Plaça Reial, and the Pont del Bisbe bridge. Wander through the ancient Roman ruins visible through glass floors at various points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to El Born neighborhood and visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina (free to enter) — a stunning market with a mosaic roof designed by Enric Miralles. Browse the stalls and grab a snack. Then explore the Palau de la Música Catalana from the outside — a UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. If budget allows, a guided tour costs €22 but the exterior is spectacular for free.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's famous nightlife. Head to El Born or the Gothic Quarter for pre-drinks at budget bars (happy hours often run 18:00–21:00 with drinks from €3–5). Later, explore the club scene — entry to many clubs is free before midnight or with a flyer. Try Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (entry €10–15 with a drink included) for a classic Barcelona club night.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastry and coffee at a traditional 'granja' (milk bar) in the Gothic Quarter (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Grab fresh food at Mercat de Santa Caterina — olives, cheese, jamón, and fruit (€6–9)
meals.dinner: Early dinner at a budget restaurant in El Born before the night out — look for a 'Menú del Día' even at dinner time (€12–15), or grab a shawarma or falafel wrap for €5–7

day_by_day.notes: Clubs in Barcelona typically don't get busy until 01:00–02:00. Many offer free entry with a drink token if you arrive before midnight. Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter — it's a tourist-heavy area with pickpockets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta beach for a morning swim and sunbathe (free). The beach is stunning in August — arrive before 10:00 to get a good spot before it gets crowded. Walk along the Passeig Marítim boardwalk and enjoy the sea breeze. Explore the Port Olímpic area and admire Frank Gehry's 'Peix d'Or' (Golden Fish) sculpture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Montjuïc — take the metro to Paral·lel and then the Funicular de Montjuïc (covered by your T-Casual card). Explore the Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (€3.50 entry) for beautiful views over the city. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for panoramic views of Barcelona, the sea, and the port. Walk back down via the cable car or funicular.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Magic Fountain of Montjuïc show (Font Màgica) — a free spectacular light, water, and music show that runs Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer (check schedule, usually starts 21:30). Afterward, head back to Eixample for drinks at a rooftop bar — many offer affordable happy hour deals with great city views.

meals.breakfast: Grab a 'croissant de mantequilla' and coffee from a beach-side kiosk or nearby café (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Eat at a chiringuito (beach bar) — try a simple 'bocadillo de calamares' or a budget paella set menu (€10–14). Avoid the most touristy spots right on the beach for better prices.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) — pasta, salad, and local wine (€5–8 total). Or grab budget street food near the Magic Fountain area.

day_by_day.notes: The Magic Fountain show schedule can vary — check the official Barcelona tourism website before heading out. Montjuïc is very exposed in August heat; visit in the late afternoon to avoid the worst of the sun. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the beach morning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau — one of Barcelona's most underrated Modernista gems designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (€16 entry, free on Sundays before 11:00 if applicable). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is just a short walk from Sagrada Família and far less crowded. Spend 1.5 hours exploring the stunning pavilions and gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Passeig de Gràcia for some final architecture spotting and window shopping. Visit the free interior courtyards of some Modernista buildings. Head to Mercat de l'Abaceria or browse local vintage and design shops in the Eixample and Gràcia neighborhoods. Pack your bags and do any last-minute souvenir shopping — look for local products like Cava, olive oil, or saffron at supermarkets for the best prices.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final farewell dinner in Eixample. Splurge slightly on your last night — try a proper sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant with Catalan cuisine: 'fideuà', 'crema catalana', or 'escalivada'. End the night with a walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia, soaking in the Modernista architecture one last time.

meals.breakfast: Full café breakfast near the hotel — coffee, juice, toast with tomato and olive oil (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Final 'Menú del Día' at a local restaurant in Eixample — make the most of this great-value tradition (€13–16)
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge farewell dinner at a Catalan restaurant — budget €20–25 per person for a proper sit-down meal with wine. Look for restaurants on side streets off Passeig de Gràcia for better value.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure details and plan transport to the airport accordingly — the Aerobus runs every 5 minutes and takes about 35 minutes. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security in August. Keep your T-Casual card for the airport metro or bus journey.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud (approx. 35–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the Eixample district to shake off travel fatigue. Walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the Block of Discord (Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, Casa Lleó Morera) from the outside — a perfect low-key introduction to Gaudí and Modernisme architecture without needing pre-booked tickets.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's legendary late dining culture. Explore the lively streets around Eixample for dinner, then grab a nightcap at a rooftop bar nearby.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample staple known for excellent tapas and montaditos at mid-range prices. Expect to queue briefly but worth it.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza (Carrer de Londres) — a relaxed, quality Eixample spot with Neapolitan-style pizzas and natural wines, easy on the wallet and no heavy commitment on arrival night.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card at the airport for cost-effective transport all week. August evenings in Barcelona are warm (25–30°C), so pack light layers for air-conditioned restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the first available morning slot (9:00 or 9:30 AM recommended). The skip-the-line guided tour lets you fully absorb Gaudí's unfinished basilica, including the towers for panoramic city views. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring the nave, facades, and crypt museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Head up to Park Güell (pre-booked timed entry required for the Monumental Zone). Marvel at the mosaic terraces and gingerbread gatehouses. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood — browse its bohemian squares (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia), indie boutiques, and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and begin the Eixample Nightlife & Cocktail Bar Crawl. Start around 10:00 PM (Barcelona standard) exploring the Gayxample triangle — bars like Bacon Bear, Plata Bar, and Quilombo offer a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere. Barcelona nightlife peaks late, so pace yourself.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament, nearby) — Aussie-inspired brunch spot with excellent coffee and avocado toast. A favorite among locals in Eixample.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Gràcia — grab supplies from Mercat de l'Abaceria or a local deli and eat in Plaça del Sol surrounded by locals. Budget-friendly and atmospheric.
meals.dinner: La Pepita (Carrer de Muntaner) — creative montaditos and pintxos in a stylish Eixample setting. Mid-range pricing, lively atmosphere, perfect pre-nightlife fuel.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance — August is peak season and slots sell out weeks ahead. Park Güell Monumental Zone also requires advance booking. Wear comfortable walking shoes; both sites involve significant walking and stairs.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Walking Tour — Take the metro to Jaume I and join a guided walking tour through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden medieval alleys. El Born extension covers the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the Born Cultural Centre with its 1714 archaeological ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Experience — Head down to Barceloneta for a relaxed beach afternoon. Swim in the Mediterranean, soak up the sun, and people-watch along the Passeig Marítim. Visit the Frank Gehry fish sculpture at the Olympic Port. Dine at a traditional chiringuito (beachside restaurant) for fresh seafood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore El Born's bar scene — one of Barcelona's most atmospheric nightlife neighborhoods. Bar del Pla, El Xampanyet (classic cava bar), and Paradiso (a speakeasy-style cocktail bar hidden behind a pastrami shop) are all within walking distance of each other.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume (Rambla de Catalunya) — classic Barcelona bakery with croissants, pastries, and strong coffee. Perfect pre-tour fuel.
meals.lunch: Chiringuito Bogatell or La Cova Fumada (Barceloneta) — La Cova Fumada is a legendary no-frills local spot credited with inventing the bombas (fried potato balls). Cash only, arrive early.
meals.dinner: Bar del Pla (El Born) — excellent Catalan tapas with a modern twist at mid-range prices. Try the foie gras with caramelized apple and the croquetas.

day_by_day.notes: August beach crowds peak in the afternoon — arrive by 1:00 PM for a good spot or visit early and move to the chiringuito for lunch. The Gothic Quarter tour is best done in the morning before heat peaks. Carry water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Deep dive into Eixample architecture — self-guided morning walk along the Modernisme route. Visit Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) with a booked ticket — La Pedrera's rooftop is especially stunning. The Eixample grid itself is an architectural marvel; look up at the chamfered corners (xamfrans) designed to ease traffic and light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill exploration — Take the cable car or Bus Turístic up to Montjuïc. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (world-class modern art, air-conditioned — perfect for a hot August afternoon), walk through the gardens, and enjoy panoramic views of the city and port from the castle.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Fountain of Montjuïc light show (check schedule — typically runs Thursday–Sunday in summer at 9:30 PM). Afterward, head to Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc for dinner and bar-hopping on Carrer de Blai (pintxos street).

meals.breakfast: Alsur Café (Eixample) — relaxed brunch spot with great eggs, granola bowls, and specialty coffee. Popular with locals and expats.
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet (Poble Sec) — a legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for creative conservas (tinned seafood) montaditos and vermut. Tiny, packed, and absolutely worth it. Lunch only.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda, Eixample) — a charming wine bar with excellent Catalan charcuterie, cheese boards, and natural wines. Relaxed mid-range setting ideal for a slower evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book La Pedrera or Casa Batlló tickets in advance. The Magic Fountain schedule varies — check the Barcelona tourism website before committing to the evening plan. Montjuïc is very exposed in August heat; go prepared with water and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Eixample — visit the Mercat de Sant Antoni (a beautifully restored 19th-century iron market) for a proper local breakfast and browse the Sunday book market if applicable. Pick up last-minute souvenirs: quality olive oil, cava, or artisan ceramics from the market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final stroll along Passeig de Gràcia for any missed architecture or shopping. Visit the Palau del Baró de Quadras or the Fundació Antoni Tàpies if time allows. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage and begin airport transfer (allow 1.5–2 hours before flight departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure — no evening activities scheduled. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final glass of cava at a rooftop bar near the hotel before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Mercat de Sant Antoni — grab a fresh orange juice, a truita (tortilla) bocadillo, and a coffee from the market bar. Authentic, local, and affordable.
meals.lunch: Parking (Carrer de Londres) or Cervecería Catalana — revisit a favorite from the week for a satisfying farewell meal. Alternatively, try Moments (if budget allows for a splurge farewell lunch).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or skip if flying early — Barcelona El Prat has decent options airside including a branch of local sandwich chain Bo de B.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully — if departing in the evening, you have more flexibility for afternoon activities. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya to Terminal 1 or 2 runs every 5–10 minutes and takes about 35 minutes. Keep metro T-Casual card for the final transfer if unused trips remain.

Take a leisurely self-guided stroll through the Eixample district to begin absorbing the neighborhood's iconic Modernista architecture — admire the chamfered corners of the city blocks (the 'Manzanas'), and pause at the façade of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside to orient yourself for deeper visits later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's nightlife with the Eixample Nightlife & Cocktail Bar Crawl. Begin at a curated selection of upscale cocktail bars in the Gayxample corridor, guided by a local expert who will introduce you to artisanal vermouths, signature gin tonics, and Barcelona's bar culture. End the night at a rooftop lounge with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or a light snack at the airport upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (Carrer de Mallorca, Eixample) — a beloved local institution just steps from the hotel, offering premium tapas, fresh seafood pintxos, and excellent Catalan craft beers in a lively setting.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza (upscale Neapolitan-style) or, for a more elevated experience, Moments at Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — a two-Michelin-star restaurant offering contemporary Catalan haute cuisine. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance through a premium car service (e.g., black Tesla or Mercedes V-Class). Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. The evening cocktail crawl is a perfect low-intensity introduction to the city's nightlife scene.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Join a skip-the-line, small-group premium guided tour of Gaudí's legendary unfinished basilica. Explore the intricate Nativity and Passion façades, ascend the towers for sweeping city views, and gain deep insight into the symbolic architecture and Gaudí's visionary genius. Allow approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Travel by private car to Park Güell to experience Gaudí's whimsical mosaic park, including the serpentine benches of the main terrace, the gingerbread gatehouses, and the Monumental Zone. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood to wander its bohemian plazas, independent boutiques, and Modernista townhouses.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and prepare for a sophisticated dinner followed by an exclusive nightlife experience. Visit one of Barcelona's premier jazz or live music bars before transitioning to an upscale club or rooftop bar in the Eixample for late-night cocktails.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament) — a stylish specialty coffee shop with avocado toast, eggs, and fresh pastries beloved by Barcelona's creative class.
meals.lunch: La Pepita (Gràcia neighborhood) — a charming, design-forward restaurant serving inventive bocadillos and seasonal Catalan dishes; perfect after exploring Gràcia.
meals.dinner: Alkimia (Carrer de la Indústria, Eixample) — a Michelin-starred restaurant by chef Jordi Vilà offering refined modern Catalan cuisine in an intimate, elegant setting. Book a tasting menu with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access tickets separately — they sell out weeks in advance. Consider a private architectural guide who specializes in Modernisme for a richer experience. Wear comfortable shoes for Park Güell, as the terrain is uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Walking Tour — Embark on a premium small-group or private guided walking tour through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city streets, the stunning Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the hidden courtyards and narrow alleys of the Barri Gòtic. Continue into El Born to visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the El Born Cultural Centre with its preserved 18th-century ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Experience — Head to Barceloneta for a relaxed luxury beach afternoon. Arrange a premium sun lounger and parasol service at a beach club (W Barcelona Beach Club or Eclipse Bar are excellent options). Enjoy the Mediterranean sun before transitioning to a traditional chiringuito or upscale beachside restaurant for fresh seafood.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the W Barcelona's Eclipse Bar on the 26th floor, offering breathtaking panoramic views over the sea and city skyline. Afterward, explore the vibrant nightlife of El Born or the Port Olímpic area, with its lively bars and clubs.

meals.breakfast: Hofmann Pastisseria (El Born) — one of Barcelona's finest pastry shops, offering exquisite croissants, ensaïmades, and specialty coffees in an elegant setting.
meals.lunch: La Mar Salada (near Barceloneta) — a refined seafood restaurant celebrated for its arroz a la marinera, grilled fish, and fresh shellfish with views of the Mediterranean.
meals.dinner: Enoteca Paco Pérez at Hotel Arts Barcelona — a two-Michelin-star restaurant offering a spectacular tasting menu focused on Mediterranean coastal cuisine, with an exceptional wine cellar and impeccable service.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored in the morning before the afternoon tourist crowds arrive. Bring sunscreen and a hat for the beach. The W Barcelona and Hotel Arts are both short taxi or rideshare rides from Eixample — approximately 15 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Deep-dive architectural day: Return to Eixample for an immersive Modernisme experience. Purchase the Ruta del Modernisme pass and visit the interiors of Casa Batlló (Book the Magic Nights or premium daytime experience with augmented reality) and Casa Milà – La Pedrera, including the extraordinary rooftop with its warrior chimneys. A private architectural guide will contextualize the genius of Domènech i Montaner, Puig i Cadafalch, and Gaudí.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana (a UNESCO World Heritage Site designed by Domènech i Montaner) on a guided tour to witness its extraordinary stained-glass interior and Art Nouveau splendor. Afterward, enjoy a leisurely afternoon shopping along Passeig de Gràcia — browse luxury boutiques including Loewe, Massimo Dutti's flagship, and local Catalan design stores.
day_by_day.evening: Experience one of Barcelona's most exclusive nightlife venues. Begin with a pre-dinner cocktail at Dry Martini Bar (Carrer d'Aribau) — an iconic, sophisticated cocktail bar with legendary martinis and a distinguished atmosphere. Then enjoy dinner before heading to an upscale club such as Sutton Club or Opium for a premium late-night experience.

meals.breakfast: Faborit or Nomad Coffee Lab in Eixample — exceptional specialty coffee with freshly baked goods and a relaxed, design-conscious atmosphere.
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda (Eixample) — a stylish wine bar and restaurant offering natural Catalan wines, charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and market-driven small plates in a warm, intimate setting.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — consistently ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants, this avant-garde culinary destination by former elBulli chefs offers a multi-course tasting menu of breathtaking creativity. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló's 'Magic Nights' rooftop experience (evenings only) is a premium add-on well worth booking. Palau de la Música Catalana tours must be pre-booked. Disfrutar reservations open months ahead — confirm this booking before the trip departs.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Eixample. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast before a final walk along Passeig de Gràcia to soak in the boulevard's grandeur one last time. Visit any remaining Modernista landmarks or pop into a gallery. Consider a visit to the Fundació Antoni Tàpies (housed in a stunning Modernista building) for a final dose of Catalan art and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (arrange late check-out if available — typically until 14:00 or 15:00 at premium properties). Enjoy a final long lunch at a celebrated Catalan restaurant before your private transfer to Barcelona–El Prat Airport. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for a comfortable, unhurried departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home. Reflect on five extraordinary days of world-class architecture, vibrant nightlife, and the incomparable energy of Barcelona.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — request a premium spread of fresh fruit, Iberian charcuterie, artisan cheeses, freshly squeezed orange juice, and specialty coffee as a luxurious farewell morning.
meals.lunch: Cinc Sentits (Carrer d'Entença, Eixample) — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering an elegant tasting menu rooted in Catalan terroir, ideal for a memorable final meal. Alternatively, Bar Calders in Sant Antoni for a more relaxed farewell tapas lunch.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport — Barcelona Airport's Terminal 1 has several quality dining options if time permits before boarding.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a premium private transfer to the airport — allow extra time in August as summer traffic near the airport can be heavy. Ask the hotel concierge to assist with last-minute gift purchases of Catalan products (cava, olive oil, local ceramics) before departure. Confirm all reservations and transfers 24 hours in advance.
